entities.name: PMID:27497908
observations: Retrospective cohort of 190 peritoneal dialysis patients; chest X-ray AoAC graded 0–3; mean follow-up 55.1 ± 32.1 months.
Grades 2 and 3 versus grade 0 predicted all-cause mortality after adjustment: HR 2.736 (95% CI 1.038–7.211) and HR 3.289 (95% CI 1.156–9.359), respectively.
Grades 2–3 predicted cardiovascular mortality after adjustment: HR 36.05 (95% CI 3.494–372); estimate is highly imprecise.
Authors concluded severe AoAC independently predicted all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in PD; later methodological commentaries were published (PMIDs 28988889 and 29208332).

entities.name: Severe AoAC predicts mortality in PD
observations: In a single retrospective PD cohort (n=190), chest-radiograph AoAC grades 2–3 were independently associated with all-cause mortality; adjusted grade-specific HRs were 2.736 and 3.289 versus grade 0.
Cardiovascular mortality association was also reported for grades 2–3, but its adjusted HR was very imprecise (36.05; 95% CI 3.494–372), limiting certainty.

entities.name: Aortic arch calcification
observations: Primary PD study measured aortic arch calcification on chest radiographs using a 0–3 severity grade.

entities.name: Peritoneal dialysis population
observations: Cohort consisted of 190 patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis.
The study reported severe aortic arch calcification as an independent mortality risk marker in this population.
